title: River Development Agent Production Execution-Package Lifecycle Orchestration Integration
objective: Establish the missing production lifecycle orchestration boundary that composes the existing authoritative execution-package creation, immutable persistence, and governed execution command boundaries into one fail-closed lifecycle, preserving the exact execution package produced by creation through persistence and executing only the persisted package through the existing DEV-329 governed execution path without reconstructing package state, duplicating lifecycle semantics, directly invoking the implementation runner, or manufacturing or broadening execution authority.

architecture.lifecycle: existing proposal, implementation-manifest, and execution-verification repository artifacts -> createExecutionPackageRiverDev -> exact resulting executionPackage object -> persistExecutionPackageRiverDev -> exact persistence repositoryPath -> executePackageRiverDev
architecture.creationBoundary: createExecutionPackageRiverDev remains the authoritative repository-safe source-artifact loading and execution-package creation boundary established and contract-hardened through DEV-330.
architecture.persistenceBoundary: persistExecutionPackageRiverDev remains the authoritative immutable persistence boundary. DEV-331 passes the exact executionPackage object returned by creation into this boundary and does not use creator serialization as a persistence contract.
architecture.executionBoundary: executePackageRiverDev remains the authoritative production persisted-package loading and governed execution boundary established by DEV-329. DEV-331 executes by passing the persistence result repositoryPath into this existing command boundary.
architecture.packageProvenance: DEV-331 must not reconstruct, normalize, repair, clone, or synthesize a second execution package between creation and persistence. The exact executionPackage object returned by createExecutionPackageRiverDev is supplied to persistExecutionPackageRiverDev. Execution subsequently reloads the persisted representation through the existing executePackageRiverDev/loadExecutionPackage boundary.
architecture.persistenceProvenance: The repositoryPath returned by authoritative persistence is the downstream package path supplied to executePackageRiverDev. DEV-331 must not independently derive or invent the persisted package path.
architecture.executionAuthority: DEV-331 creates, acquires, upgrades, synthesizes, broadens, or repairs no execution authorization. Any preexisting operationExecutionAuthorization accepted by the lifecycle is forwarded unchanged to executePackageRiverDev. Requested apply mode alone is never authorization.
architecture.execution: DEV-331 does not directly call createImplementationRunner, runner.execute, executePackage, DEV-326, DEV-327, or DEV-328. Governed execution remains owned by executePackageRiverDev and its established DEV-329 chain.
architecture.failureSemantics: Lifecycle stages are strictly ordered and fail closed. Creation failure prevents persistence and execution. Persistence failure prevents execution. Governed execution failure propagates without fallback or alternate execution.
architecture.mutationSemantics: Creation performs no implementation writes. Persistence may create only the immutable execution-package artifact through its existing create-only contract. Implementation repository mutation, if any, may occur only downstream through executePackageRiverDev when independently authorized apply execution is admitted.
architecture.determinism: For identical authoritative inputs and equivalent repository state, lifecycle composition must preserve deterministic package creation and established deterministic downstream behavior. DEV-331 introduces no nondeterministic package reconstruction.
architecture.legacyImplementBoundary: DEV-331 does not rewrite, remove, or reroute implementRiverDevPlan. Reconciliation of the legacy direct-manifest implementation path is a later explicit integration boundary after the canonical package lifecycle exists and is proven.
architecture.defaultDeny: Missing, inaccessible, malformed, inconsistent, unapproved, unverified, non-ready, non-persistable, already-persisted-conflicting, unauthorized, or otherwise invalid lifecycle state must fail closed through the authoritative stage that owns that validation.

invariants: No second execution-package creator or representation is introduced.
No second persistence implementation or persistence-path derivation is introduced.
No second persisted-package loader is introduced.
No execution package is reconstructed between creation and persistence.
Creator serialization is not treated as the persistence contract.
The exact created executionPackage object is supplied to authoritative persistence.
The authoritative persistence repositoryPath is supplied to executePackageRiverDev.
No direct implementation runner invocation is permitted from DEV-331.
No direct executePackage invocation is permitted from DEV-331.
DEV-331 does not bypass DEV-329, DEV-328, DEV-327, or DEV-326.
DEV-331 does not create, reacquire, synthesize, upgrade, broaden, or repair execution authorization.
Apply intent alone never grants execution authority.
Creation failure stops persistence and execution.
Implementation writes can occur only through independently authorized governed execution.
Legacy implementRiverDevPlan remains unchanged by DEV-331.
acceptanceCriteria: A production lifecycle command accepts repository paths for the existing proposal, implementation manifest, and execution verification artifacts plus execution mode and optional preexisting operation execution authorization.
The lifecycle delegates source loading and package creation to createExecutionPackageRiverDev rather than loading or constructing those artifacts independently.
The exact executionPackage object returned by creation is passed to persistExecutionPackageRiverDev.
The lifecycle uses the repositoryPath returned by persistence as the package path passed to executePackageRiverDev.
Dry-run lifecycle execution requires no manufactured apply authorization and remains governed by the existing execution chain.
Apply lifecycle execution cannot succeed merely because apply mode was requested and requires authorization already accepted by the existing governed execution boundary.
Creation-stage rejection prevents persistence and execution.
Governed execution rejection propagates without direct-runner or alternate-executor fallback.
The lifecycle performs no direct implementation runner invocation and does not duplicate package-executor semantics.
Immutable persistence remains authoritative and conflicting overwrite attempts fail closed.
The lifecycle exposes sufficient result provenance to identify creation, persistence, and governed execution outcomes without creating a second package representation.

Tests prove valid dry-run lifecycle composition, exact created-package handoff, persistence-path handoff, creation failure short-circuiting, persistence failure short-circuiting, unauthorized apply rejection, authorized apply forwarding without authority modification, no direct runner/executor bypass, and deterministic lifecycle behavior.
